• The combustion of coal is an example of Combination Reaction.
 
• A combination reaction is a reaction where two or more elements or compounds combine to form a single compound. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: X + Y → XY.
 
• The combination of two or more elements to form one compound is called a combination reaction.

• The opposite of a combination reaction, a complex molecule breaks down to make simpler ones. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: AB → A + B.
 
 
 
• Precipitation reaction__: 
 __
 
• Two solutions of soluble salts are mixed resulting in an insoluble solid (precipitate) forming. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: A + Soluble salt B → Precipitate + soluble salt C.
 
 
 
• Neutralization reaction__: 
 __
 
• An acid and a base react with each other. Generally, the product of this reaction is salt and water. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: Acid + Base → Salt + Water.

• Oxygen combines with a compound to form carbon dioxide and water. These reactions are exothermic, meaning they give off heat. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: A + O2 → H2O + CO2.
 
 
 
• Displacement reaction__: 
 __
 
• One element takes place with another element in the compound. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: A + BC → AC + B.
 
 
 
• Double displacement reaction__:
 
 
• Double displacement reactions occur when a part of two ionic compounds is exchanged and makes two new components.
 
• Double displacement reactions take place mostly in aqueous solutions wherein the ions precipitate and the exchange of ions takes place.

questions.question: In 1808, whose work provided a physical picture of how compounds are formed by the combination of two or more different types of atoms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**John Dalton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• John Dalton was an English chemist, physicist, and meteorologist who is best known for his pioneering work in the development of modern atomic theory.
 
• Dalton's atomic theory, which he proposed in** 1808**, provided a physical picture of how compounds are formed by the **combination of two or more different types of atoms**.
 
• He suggested that all matter is made up of tiny, indivisible particles called atoms, which combine in fixed ratios to form compounds.
 
• His theory was based on several key principles, including the idea that atoms of different elements have different weights and properties, that atoms can combine to form molecules, and that chemical reactions involve the rearrangement of atoms.
 
• Dalton's work on atomic theory was groundbreaking and laid the foundation for modern chemistry.
 
• He was also the first scientist to study the **behavior of gases** and to develop a method for **measuring the relative weights of atoms**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**George Zweig**

 
• He proposed the concept of quarks in **1964**, which are subatomic particles that makeup protons and neutrons.
 
• He suggested that quarks come in six different "flavors" and that they are held together by a strong nuclear force.
 
• **Joseph J Thomson**
 
• He discovered the **electron **in **1897 **while studying cathode rays.
 
• He proposed the plum pudding model of the atom, which suggested that atoms were made up of a positively charged substance with negatively charged electrons embedded in it.

**Niels Bohr**

 
• He developed the Bohr model of the atom in **1913**, which proposed that electrons orbit the **nucleus at fixed energy levels**.
 
• He also suggested that electrons can jump between energy levels by **absorbing or emitting energy in the form of photons**.

questions.question: For a chemical reaction with rise in temperature by 10°, the rate constant becomes nearly ________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Double**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• For many chemical reactions, the rate constant approximately doubles with a 10°C increase in temperature.
 
• This phenomenon is often referred to as the "rule of thumb" in chemical kinetics.
 
• The temperature dependence of the rate constant is described by the Arrhenius equation.
 
• According to the Arrhenius equation, the rate constant (k) is related to temperature (T) through the exponential factor involving activation energy (Ea) and the gas constant (R).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arrhenius Equation:**

 
 
• The Arrhenius equation is k = A * exp(-Ea/(RT)), where k is the rate constant, A is the pre-exponential factor (frequency of collisions), Ea is the activation energy, R is the gas constant, and T is the temperature in Kelvin.
 
• This equation shows the relationship between the rate constant and temperature, indicating that as temperature increases, the rate constant increases exponentially.
 
 
 
• **Activation Energy (Ea):**
 
 
• Activation energy is the minimum energy that reacting molecules must possess to undergo a chemical reaction.
 
• Higher activation energy means that fewer molecules have sufficient energy to react at a given temperature.
 
 
 
• **Gas Constant (R):**
 
 
• The gas constant (R) is a physical constant that appears in many fundamental equations in physical sciences, such as the ideal gas law and the Arrhenius equation.
 
• The value of R is 8.314 J/(mol·K).
 
 
 
• **Rule of Thumb in Chemical Kinetics:**
 
 
• The "rule of thumb" in chemical kinetics suggests that for many reactions, the rate constant approximately doubles for every 10°C rise in temperature.
 
• This empirical rule helps chemists estimate the effect of temperature changes on reaction rates without detailed calculations.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most acidic?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**HCOOH**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• HCOOH, also known as formic acid, is the simplest carboxylic acid and is the most acidic among the given options.
 
• Formic acid has the highest acidity due to the absence of electron-donating alkyl groups which decrease the acidity by destabilizing the conjugate base.
 
• The other options, such as C2H5COOH (propanoic acid), C3H7COOH (butanoic acid), and CH3COOH (acetic acid), have alkyl groups that reduce their acidity.
 
• Formic acid is widely used in various industrial processes and has a higher acid dissociation constant (Ka) compared to other carboxylic acids listed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carboxylic Acids**

 
 
• Carboxylic acids are organic acids characterized by the presence of a carboxyl group (–COOH).
 
• The acidity of carboxylic acids is due to the resonance stabilization of the carboxylate anion (R-COO−) formed after deprotonation.
 
• Electron-withdrawing groups increase acidity by stabilizing the carboxylate anion, while electron-donating groups decrease acidity by destabilizing it.
 
 
 
• **Acid Dissociation Constant (Ka)**
 
 
• The acid dissociation constant (Ka) is a quantitative measure of the strength of an acid in solution.
 
• It is the equilibrium constant for the dissociation of an acid into its conjugate base and a proton (H⁺).
 
• Higher Ka values indicate stronger acids, as they dissociate more completely in solution.
 
• Formic acid has a higher Ka value compared to the other carboxylic acids listed, making it more acidic.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing Acidity**
 
 
• Inductive Effect: Electron-withdrawing groups increase acidity, while electron-donating groups decrease it.
 
• Resonance Effect: Resonance stabilization of the conjugate base increases acidity.
 
• Hybridization: Acidity increases with the s-character of the hybrid orbital holding the acidic hydrogen (sp > sp² > sp³).
 
• Solvation: Better solvation of the conjugate base in a solvent increases acidity.

questions.question: According to which of the following laws, the pressure of a mixture of gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of the component gases?

The correct answer is __**Dalton's Law**__.

__
 
• **Dalton's Law:**

 
 
• **Definition: **Dalton's Law, also known as the Law of Partial Pressures, states that **the total pressure exerted by a mixture of gases is the sum of the partial pressures of the individual gases.**
 
• **Partial Pressure: **The pressure that each gas would exert if it alone occupied the entire volume of the mixture is its partial pressure.
 
• **Independent Behaviour: **The law assumes that gases behave independently of each other, meaning the pressure of each gas in a mixture is unaffected by the presence of other gases.
 
• **Applications: **Dalton's Law has important applications in many areas including chemistry, physics, physiology, and even scuba diving, where understanding the pressures of different gas components is crucial.

questions.question: ______ states that the rates of diffusion of gases are inversely proportional to the square roots of their densities under similar conditions of temperature and pressure.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Graham's Law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Graham's law** states that the rates of **diffusion of gases are inversely proportional to the square roots of their molar masses under similar conditions of temperature and pressure.**
 
• This means that a gas with a lower molar mass will diffuse more quickly than a gas with a higher molar mass.
 
• **For example, hydrogen (H2) has a molar mass of 2.016 g/mol, while oxygen (O2) has a molar mass of 32.000 g/mol.**
 
• This means that hydrogen will diffuse **4.5 times faster than oxygen at the same temperature and pressure.**
 
• Graham's law can be used to calculate the rate of diffusion of a gas.
 
• **The formula for Graham's law is: r = k * √(M)**
 
• **Where**:
 
 
• **r **is the rate of **diffusion**
 
• **k **is a **constant**
 
• **M** is the** molar mass of the gas**
 
 
 
• **The value of k can be determined experimentally.**
 
• **Graham's law** is a useful tool for understanding the behaviour of gases.
 
• **It can be used to predict how gases will diffuse, and it can be used to calculate the rate of diffusion of a gas.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Tyndall's Law** states that the scattering of a beam of light by particles in a** medium is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength of ligh**t.

 
 
• This means that shorter wavelengths of** light are scattered more easily than longer wavelengths.**
 
 
 
• **Pascal's Law** states that pressure exerted anywhere in an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally in all directions throughout the fluid.
 
 
• This means that if you increase the** pressure at one point in a fluid, the pressure will increase at all points in the fluid.**
 
 
 
• **Kepler's Laws** are three laws that describe the motion of planets around the sun.

questions.question: The type of reaction that is typically found when a material that is required for the reaction to proceed, such as a surface or a catalyst, is saturated by the reactants is called a ________ order reaction.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**zero**__ order reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a **zero-order reaction**, the rate of reaction is **independent of the concentration of the reactants**.
 
• These reactions are commonly seen in **catalytic processes** where the catalyst surface is saturated by the reactants.
 
• In such reactions, the rate of reaction remains constant until the **reactant concentration is significantly depleted**.
 
• Zero-order kinetics is often observed in **heterogeneous catalysis** and other situations where a limiting step is saturated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First-order Reaction**

 
 
• A first-order reaction is one where the rate is directly proportional to the concentration of one reactant.
 
• The rate law for a first-order reaction can be expressed as: Rate = k[A], where k is the rate constant and [A] is the concentration of the reactant.
 
• These reactions often involve unimolecular processes.
 
• Examples include radioactive decay and certain substitution reactions in organic chemistry.
 
 
 
• **Second-order Reaction**
 
 
• A second-order reaction's rate is proportional to the square of the concentration of one reactant or the product of the concentrations of two reactants.
 
• The rate law can be written as: Rate = k[A]² or Rate = k[A][B], depending on the reaction mechanism.
 
• These reactions often involve bimolecular processes.
 
• Examples include the reaction between hydrogen and iodine to form hydrogen iodide.
 
 
 
• **Third-order Reaction**
 
 
• A third-order reaction's rate depends on the concentration of three reactants or the concentration of one reactant raised to the third power, or other combinations summing to three.
 
• The rate law can be expressed as: Rate = k[A]³ or other combinations.
 
• These reactions are less common compared to first and second-order reactions.
 
• An example is the reaction between nitric oxide and oxygen to form nitrogen dioxide.

questions.question: Which property of an element is inversely related to its ionisation energy?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ionisation energy** is the energy required to remove an electron from an atom in its gaseous state.
 
• The **atomic radius** is the distance from the nucleus of an atom to the outermost electron shell.
 
• As the **atomic radius** increases, the attraction between the nucleus and the electrons decreases.
 
• This decreased attraction makes it easier to remove an electron, resulting in lower **ionisation energy**.
 
• Therefore, there is an **inverse relationship** between the atomic radius and ionisation energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electronegativity**__

 __
 
• **Electronegativity** is a measure of an atom's ability to attract and hold onto electrons.
 
• Elements with high electronegativity have a strong attraction for electrons.
 
• Typically, electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group in the periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Atomic mass**__
 __
 
• **Atomic mass** is the mass of an atom, usually expressed in atomic mass units (amu).
 
• It is approximately equivalent to the number of protons and neutrons in the atom (mass number).
 
• Atomic mass does not have a direct relationship with ionisation energy.
 
 
 
• **Electron affinity**__
 
 
• **Electron affinity** is the energy change that occurs when an electron is added to a neutral atom in the gaseous state.
 
• It is generally exothermic, meaning energy is released when an electron is added.
 
• Elements with high electron affinity values are more likely to gain electrons.

questions.question: The process of depositing a layer of any desired metal on another material by means of electricity is called ____________.

The correct answer is __**electroplating**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Electroplating is a process used to coat the surface of a metal with a thin layer of another metal using an electric current.
 
• It is commonly used for decorative purposes, corrosion protection, and to improve wear resistance.
 
• The process involves immersing both the item to be plated and the plating metal in an electrolyte solution and applying a current.
 
• The plating metal acts as the anode, and the item to be plated acts as the cathode, causing metal ions to move and deposit on the item.
 
• Materials commonly used for electroplating include gold, silver, nickel, and chromium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrolysis:**

 
 
• Electrolysis is a broader term that refers to the decomposition of a substance by passing an electric current through it.
 
• It is used in various applications, including electroplating, electrorefining, and electrolysis of water to produce hydrogen and oxygen.
 
 
 
• **Anode and Cathode:**
 
 
• In electroplating, the anode is the metal that will be deposited, and the cathode is the item that is being plated.
 
• The anode is positively charged, while the cathode is negatively charged.
 
 
 
• **Electrolyte Solution:**
 
 
• The electrolyte solution is a liquid that contains ions and conducts electricity, facilitating the movement of metal ions from the anode to the cathode.
 
• Common electrolytes include solutions of metal salts, such as copper sulfate for copper plating.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Electroplating:**
 
 
• Electroplating is used in various industries, including automotive, jewelry, electronics, and aerospace.
 
• It enhances the appearance, durability, and conductivity of the plated items.

questions.question: In 1960, which isotope was used to define the standard measure of length?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krypton-86**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Krypton-86** was used in 1960 to define the standard measure of length.
 
• The length of the meter was defined based on the wavelength of the radiation emitted by Krypton-86.
 
• This definition was adopted by the 11th General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM) in 1960.
 
• It was later replaced in 1983 by the definition based on the speed of light.
 
• The use of Krypton-86 provided a more precise and reproducible standard compared to the previous definitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM)** is the international authority responsible for uniformity in measurements.
 
• In 1983, the meter was redefined as the distance light travels in a vacuum in 1/299,792,458 seconds.
 
• This new definition ties the unit of length directly to a fundamental constant of nature, the speed of light.
 
• The redefinition aimed to increase the precision and universality of the meter as a unit of measure.

questions.question: Calculate the oxidation number of 'S' in H₂S₂O₇.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__.

• Let's denote the oxidation number of sulfur as 'x'.
 
• In H₂S₂O₇:
 
• Hydrogen (H) has an oxidation number of +1.
 
• Oxygen (O) has an oxidation number of -2.
 
• The overall charge of the molecule is 0.
 
• So, we can set up the equation: 
 
• 2(+1) + 2(x) + 7(-2) = 0
 
• Simplifying:
 
• 2 + 2x - 14 = 0
 
• 2x = 12
 
• x = +6 
 
• Therefore, the oxidation number of sulfur (S) in H₂S₂O₇ is **+6.**

questions.question: Identify the correct statement about nuclear fission.

options.text: The nucleus of a heavy atom, when bombarded with low-energy neutrons, can be split apart into lighter nuclei.
Nuclear fission is the coming together of high-energy electrons and low-energy neutrons.
The nucleus of a low-energy atom, when bombarded with high-energy neutrons, can be split apart into lighter nuclei.
The nucleus of a low-energy atom, when bombarded with high-energy neutrons, can be split apart into heavier nuclei.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The nucleus of a heavy atom, when bombarded with low-energy neutrons, can be split apart into lighter nuclei.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nuclear fission** is a process in which the nucleus of a** heavy atom is split **into lighter nuclei.
 
• This process is usually initiated by **bombarding the heavy nucleus** with **low-energy neutrons.**
 
• The splitting of the nucleus releases a** large amount of energy** in the form of** heat and radiation,** which can be harnessed for practical purposes.
 
• Nuclear fission is used in **nuclear power plants** to generate electricity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nuclear fusion** is coming together of **high-energy electrons** and **low-energy neutrons. **
 
• The nucleus of a low-energy atom is not heavy enough to **undergo fission.** 
 
• Only heavy nuclei, such as **uranium and plutonium**, are **capable of fission.**
 
• Nucleus of a low-energy atom cannot be **split apart into heavier nuclei.**

questions.question: When you take Lead nitrate powder in a boiling tube and heat it, you will observe the emission of brown fumes that are of _________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitrogen dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nitrogen dioxide (NO₂)** is a brown gas that is emitted when lead nitrate is heated.
 
• Lead nitrate decomposes to form lead oxide (PbO), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), and oxygen (O₂).
 
• The chemical reaction for this process is:

 **2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂**.
 
• The brown fumes observed during the heating of lead nitrate are characteristic of nitrogen dioxide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lead Nitrate (Pb(NO₃)₂)**:

 
 
• It is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula Pb(NO₃)₂.
 
• It is soluble in water and is commonly used in laboratories and industries.
 
• When heated, lead nitrate decomposes into lead oxide, nitrogen dioxide, and oxygen.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂)**:
 
 
• It is a reddish-brown gas with a characteristic sharp, biting odor.
 
• It is one of several nitrogen oxides and is a significant air pollutant.
 
• NO₂ is a major component of smog and can have harmful effects on the respiratory system.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Reactions**:
 
 
• In chemistry, a chemical reaction is a process that leads to the transformation of one set of chemical substances to another.
 
• Reactions involve the breaking of bonds in reactants and the formation of new bonds in products.
 
• Decomposition reactions, like the heating of lead nitrate, involve the breakdown of a single compound into two or more simpler substances.

questions.question: ______ states that for a solution of volatile liquids, the partial vapour pressure of each component of the solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction present in solution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raoult’s law**__.

**Raoult’s law** states that a solvent’s partial vapour pressure in a solution (or mixture) is equal or identical to the vapour pressure of the pure solvent multiplied by its mole fraction in the solution.

Mathematically, Raoult’s law equation is written as;

Pₛₒₗᵤₜᵢₒₙ = ΧₛₒₗvₑₙₜP⁰ₛₒₗvₑₙₜ

Where,

Psolution = vapour pressure of the solution

Χₛₒₗvₑₙₜ = mole fraction of the solvent

P⁰ₛₒₗvₑₙₜ = vapour pressure of the pure solvent

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
 

 Boyle’s law
 
 
 
• Boyle’s law, also called Mariotte’s law, a relation concerning the compression and expansion of a gas at a constant temperature.
 
• The pressure exerted by a gas (of a given mass, kept at a constant temperature) is inversely proportional to the volume occupied by it.
 
• The pressure (P) of a given quantity of gas varies inversely with its volume (V) at constant temperature; i.e., in equation form, PV = k, a constant.

• The Law of Partial Pressures, states that the total pressure exerted by a mixture of gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of the gases in the mixture.

questions.question: Which of the following is a molecular compound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CO₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **CO₂ (Carbon Dioxide)** is a molecular compound because it is formed by covalent bonding between carbon and oxygen atoms.
 
• Molecular compounds are typically composed of nonmetals. CO₂ consists of two nonmetals: carbon and oxygen.
 
• The carbon atom in CO₂ shares its electrons with two oxygen atoms, forming double covalent bonds, which is characteristic of molecular compounds.
 
• CO₂ exists as discrete molecules in its gaseous state, unlike ionic compounds which form a lattice structure.
 
• It is not an ionic compound like NaCl or MgSO₄, which are composed of ions, nor a metallic compound like CaO.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Molecular Compounds:**

 
 
• Molecular compounds are made of nonmetals and are held together by covalent bonds, where electrons are shared between atoms.
 
• They typically have lower melting and boiling points compared to ionic compounds.
 
• Examples include CO₂, H₂O, and CH₄.
 
 
 
• **Ionic Compounds:**
 
 
• Ionic compounds are formed by the transfer of electrons between metals and nonmetals, resulting in positive and negative ions.
 
• Examples include NaCl, MgSO₄, and CaO.
 
• They usually have high melting and boiling points and form a crystal lattice structure.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂):**
 
 
• CO₂ is a greenhouse gas that is a major contributor to global warming and climate change.
 
• It is released through natural processes such as respiration and volcanic eruptions, as well as human activities like burning fossil fuels.
 
• It is used in various applications, including carbonated beverages, fire extinguishers, and as a refrigerant.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Oxide (CaO):**
 
 
• Commonly known as quicklime, it is an ionic compound formed by calcium and oxygen.
 
• It is used in cement production, soil stabilization, and as a chemical reagent.
